cases.title: Compute I/Y for a 30-year $75,000 mortgage with $425.84 monthly payments
cases.notes: Example does not press RESET; it relies on the machine being in default state, so FV=0 and END are preconditions rather than keystrokes. The 2ND P/Y 12 ENTER step sets C/Y=12 implicitly. PV positive (money received by borrower), PMT negative (money paid out) - the required sign change avoids Error 5.

cases.title: Compute monthly PMT on a $75,000 30-year mortgage at 5.5%
cases.notes: No RESET; FV=0 and END are assumed preconditions. Result negative: computed outflow.

cases.title: Compute quarterly PMT on the same $75,000 30-year loan at 5.5%
cases.notes: Deliberately inherits I/Y and PV from tvm-monthly-loan-payment - the guidebook notes the calculator saves entered values for later use. Only reproducible if that case ran first; the inherited values are therefore encoded in setup. Setting P/Y=4 also sets C/Y=4.

cases.title: Compute FV of a $5,000 deposit after 20 years at 0.5% annual
cases.notes: RESET establishes the whole setup (P/Y=C/Y=1, END, DEC=2, CHN) and displays RST then 0.00. PV negative (money paid into the account), FV positive (money received back). PMT is left at its reset default of 0 - the unused fifth variable.

cases.title: Compute PV needed to reach $10,000 in 20 years at 0.5% annual
cases.notes: Continues directly from tvm-savings-future-value, inheriting N=20, I/Y=0.5 and PMT=0; only FV is re-entered. Result negative: the deposit is an outflow.

cases.title: PV of $20,000 annual savings over 10 years at 10% (ordinary annuity)
cases.notes: Furros Company example. P/Y=C/Y=1 after RESET, so I/Y=10 is both the annual and the per-period rate. PMT entered negative, PV computed positive. FV stays at its reset default of 0.

cases.title: PV of the same $20,000 x 10yr @10% stream as an annuity due
cases.notes: Continues from tvm-pv-ordinary-annuity, changing only the payment timing. The BGN indicator lights; no indicator is shown for END. Ratio to the ordinary annuity is exactly (1+i) = 1.10, confirming Gi = 1 + i x 1.

cases.title: Price of a perpetual bond paying $110/yr to yield 15% (ordinary annuity)
cases.notes: Land of Oz example. NOT a TVM worksheet calculation - executed purely on the arithmetic keys and must not be routed through the TVM solver. The % key converts 15 to 0.15 as a postfix unary operator; 110/0.15 = 733.33. Result is positive (a price), contrary to the TVM outflow-negative convention. Identical under CHN and AOS - no precedence conflict.

cases.title: Price of the same perpetual bond as an annuity due
cases.notes: Chains directly off the 733.33 left on the display by tvm-perpetual-ordinary-annuity: PV = PMT + PMT/((I/Y)/100), i.e. 110 + 733.33. Arithmetic keys only.

cases.title: PV of a $5,000 cash flow received in year 1 at 10%
cases.notes: ABC Company example. Unequal cash flows are handled on the TVM worksheet by discounting each one separately as a lump sum (PMT=0 after RESET) and summing in memory. Cash flow entered as negative FV so the computed PV comes back positive.

cases.title: PV of a $7,000 cash flow received in year 2 at 10%
cases.notes: Continues from year 1; STO 1 banks the prior 4,545.45 first. I/Y and PMT=0 inherited.

cases.title: PV of an $8,000 cash flow received in year 3 at 10%
cases.notes: STO + 1 accumulates the year-2 PV into memory 1 before the year-3 solve.

cases.title: PV of a $10,000 cash flow received in year 4 at 10%
cases.notes: STO + 1 accumulates the year-3 PV into memory 1 before the year-4 solve.

cases.title: Recall the summed present value of all four cash flows
cases.notes: CRITICAL PRECISION TEST. Memory must accumulate UNROUNDED values. The four exact PVs are 4545.4545454545, 5785.1239669421, 6010.5184072126 and 6830.1345536507, summing to 23171.2314732600 -> displays 23,171.23. Summing the four DISPLAYED (rounded) values gives 23,171.22 and fails. setup.M1 is the running total after the first three STO operations.

cases.title: Subtract the machine's $23,000 cost from the total present value
cases.notes: Chains off the unrounded 23,171.2314... recalled from memory. Answer: the PV exceeds cost by $171.23, so the investment is profitable. Rounding the recalled value to 23,171.23 first still yields 171.23 here, but the unrounded path is the correct model.

cases.title: PV of a $6,500 residual value, 46 months at 22% compounded monthly, BGN
cases.notes: CRITICAL PRECISION TEST. P/Y=C/Y=1 after RESET, so the PERIODIC rate is keyed directly: 22 DIV 12 EQUALS = 1.8333333... The display reads 1.83 but the stored value keeps full precision. Storing the displayed 1.83 instead makes the downstream lease total 40,601.33 rather than 40,573.18.

cases.title: PV of a lease: $1,200 x 46 monthly payments plus $6,500 residual, BGN
cases.notes: Continues from tvm-lease-residual-present-value; adding PMT re-solves PV for residual + payment stream together. Answer: Peach Bright pays $40,573.18. setup.I/Y carries the unrounded 22/12.

cases.title: Monthly PMT financing $525 at 20% APR compounded monthly over 2 years
cases.notes: Desk and chair example. RESET forces P/Y back to 1, which is why P/Y=12 must be re-entered immediately after. 2 2ND xP/Y N gives N=24. FV=0 from RESET.

cases.title: FV of $200 deposited at the start of each month for 20 years at 7.5%
cases.notes: Annuity due - interest accrues from the start of each period, giving a slightly higher yield than END. PV=0 from RESET (the unused fifth variable). PMT negative (deposits paid in), FV positive (balance received).

cases.title: Loan amount affordable at $325/month for 48 months at 7.5% APR
cases.notes: Car purchase example. 4 2ND xP/Y N gives N=48. FV=0 from RESET. PMT negative, PV computed positive (the borrower receives the loan).

cases.title: Down payment required on a $15,100 car after borrowing $13,441.47
cases.notes: Chains off the computed PV still on the display: 13,441.47 + (-15,100) = -1,658.53. Negative because the down payment is an outflow. Answer stated as $1,658.53.

cases.title: Monthly BGN deposit to reach $25,000 in 10 years at 0.5% with quarterly compounding
cases.notes: The only example in range where P/Y != C/Y. Order is load-bearing: entering P/Y=12 auto-writes C/Y=12, so C/Y=4 must be set AFTERWARDS via the DOWN key inside the same worksheet. The guidebook flags this trap explicitly. PV=0 from RESET. i = (1+0.005/4)^(4/12)-1 = 0.00041649 per month.

cases.title: Monthly PMT on a $120,000 30-year loan at 6.125% APR
cases.notes: CRITICAL PRECISION TEST and the section's sign-convention arbiter. Keying 6.125 I/Y DISPLAYS 6.13 but STORES 6.125; storing the displayed 6.13 yields -729.52 and fails. The printed appendix PMT formula (p. 75) omits its leading minus sign and evaluates to +729.132647 (displaying 729.13) - the calculator displays -729.13, so the worked example wins and the formula needs a leading minus. Magnitude as printed is correct; only the sign is wrong.

cases.title: Loan balance after payment 9 (first year, April start) on the $120,000 mortgage
cases.notes: First payment is in April, so the first year spans only 9 periods. Amortization uses PMT ROUNDED to 2 decimals (-729.13), not the unrounded -729.132647 - this is the documented BAL/FV divergence.

cases.title: Principal paid over payments 1-9 on the $120,000 mortgage
cases.notes: PRN = bal(9) - bal(0) = 118,928.63 - 120,000.00. The printed appendix formula says bal(pmt2) - bal(pmt1), which gives -954.74 and is WRONG; it must be bal(pmt2) - bal(pmt1 - 1). Guidebook typesets this value as '-1071.37' without a thousands separator while '-1,507.03' in the same column has one; the calculator's US format inserts separators uniformly, so the separator form is used here.

cases.title: Interest paid over payments 1-9 on the $120,000 mortgage
cases.notes: INT = (9-1+1) x (-729.13) - (-1,071.37) = -6,562.17 + 1,071.37. Negative: interest is an outflow, matching the PMT sign. Note the trailing zero - display must not be truncated to -5,490.8.

cases.title: Loan balance after payment 21 (second year) on the $120,000 mortgage
cases.notes: Per-period rounding check. bal(m) = bal(m-1) - I_m + RND(PMT) with I_m = RND[RND12(-i x bal(m-1))]. The load-bearing detail is the OUTER RND on I_m: because bal(0)=RND(PV), I_m and RND(PMT) are all at 2 decimals, the running balance lands on 2 decimals by construction, so the explicit re-rounding of bal(m) is a no-op here rather than a separate requirement. Dropping the outer RND on I_m and letting the balance carry sub-cent precision gives 118,928.64 / 117,421.62 / 115,819.66 - it fails the FIRST range too, not just this one. In the guidebook the range is reached by pressing DOWN from INT to wrap back to P1.

cases.title: Principal paid over payments 10-21 on the $120,000 mortgage
cases.notes: PRN = bal(21) - bal(9) = 117,421.60 - 118,928.63. Confirms the off-by-one correction: the printed bal(pmt2) - bal(pmt1) would give -1,384.93.

cases.title: Interest paid over payments 10-21 on the $120,000 mortgage
CPT on P1 auto-advances the amortization window to the third year
cases.notes: Tests auto-advance. From INT, DOWN wraps to P1; CPT then advances BOTH P1 and P2 to the next window, preserving the 12-period width (10-21 becomes 22-33). The DOWN keys walk P1->P2->BAL->PRN->INT then wrap.

cases.title: P2 after auto-advancing the amortization window to the third year
cases.notes: P2 was recomputed automatically by the CPT on P1; the guidebook notes it can still be overwritten.

cases.title: Loan balance after payment 33 (third year) on the $120,000 mortgage
cases.notes: Third range of the same per-period-rounding check as amort-year2-balance; the rounding error accumulates from the origin, so this range is the most sensitive. Dropping the outer RND on I_m gives 115,819.66 here (4 cents high).

cases.title: Principal paid over payments 22-33 on the $120,000 mortgage
cases.notes: PRN = bal(33) - bal(21) = 115,819.62 - 117,421.60. Guidebook typesets this as '-1601.98' without a thousands separator; the separator form is used here to match the calculator's uniform US display format.

cases.title: Interest paid over payments 22-33 on the $120,000 mortgage
Monthly PMT on an $82,000 property loan at 7% over a 30-year amortization
cases.notes: Seller-financing example: amortized over 30 years but with a balloon due after 5. Unrounded PMT is -545.5480460469...

cases.title: Balloon payment: balance due after 5 years on the $82,000 loan
cases.notes: Demonstrates xP/Y used INSIDE the Amortization worksheet: 5 2ND xP/Y = 60 months, committed to P2 with ENTER. P1 is 1 from the preceding RESET default. Amortization uses the rounded PMT of -545.55.

cases.title: Total interest received over the first 5 years on the $82,000 loan
cases.notes: DISCREPANCY - the guidebook's own prose contradicts its table. The worked table displays INT= -27,920.72; the bullet list below it says $27,790.72 (two digits transposed). The TABLE WINS: 60 x 545.55 = 32,733.00 total paid, PRN = 82,000 - 77,187.72 = 4,812.28, so INT = 27,920.72. Reached by DOWN DOWN from BAL, skipping past the PRN display.
